title: Shopping Trajectory Representation Learning with Pre-training for E-commerce Customer Understanding and Recommendation

problem.claim: Improving service quality in large-scale e-commerce requires understanding customer behavior.

contributions.claim: C-STAR learns compact customer representations from shopping journeys for multiple downstream customer-centric tasks.
The framework defines shopping trajectories over product-category interactions and models both inter-trajectory distribution similarity and intra-trajectory semantic correlation.
The framework introduces a pre-training strategy designed to capture two intrinsic properties of the pre-training data.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present C-STAR as a new framework and introduce a pre-training strategy for improving trajectory embeddings.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive evaluation on large-scale industrial and public datasets across three diverse customer-centric tasks.
The authors report that C-STAR demonstrates effectiveness across the evaluated tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Customer behavior understanding is framed as important for improving large-scale e-commerce service quality.
C-STAR is proposed to learn compact representations from customer shopping journeys.
Shopping trajectories are defined over product-category interactions, with modeling of structural similarity across trajectories and semantic correlation within trajectories.
A coarse-to-fine representation approach and a pre-training strategy are used to improve embedding quality.
The framework is evaluated on industrial and public datasets for three customer-centric tasks supporting profiling and recommendation services.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines trajectory-level structural similarity with within-trajectory semantic correlation.

interpretation.claim: Modeling relationships both across complete behavior sequences and within individual sequences may produce more informative customer representations.

application.claim: For sequential customer-behavior representation tasks, consider combining global sequence-relationship modeling with local semantic modeling.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this combination is necessary or effective outside the reported customer-centric tasks and datasets.

unknowns: The specific two intrinsic pre-training properties are not described.
The three evaluated tasks, datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not specified.
The abstract does not describe implementation details, computational costs, limitations, or failure cases.
